result:
I've saved the Q3 results to `/work/answer.json`. Before calculating Q3, I ran the same method on Q2 and it reproduced all 10 of your reference values exactly.

```json
{"a_segment": "smb", "a_net": 300014989, "b_customers": 249, "c_category": "acc", "c_net": 254927660,
 "d_month": "2025-08", "e_email": "u198@ex.com", "f_repeat": 232, "g_avg": 703377, "h_growth": -6.3}
```

The definitions you gave weren't quite enough to match the Q2 values. I needed three extra rules:
1. **Time zone:** `ordered_at` is stored in UTC (`...Z`). I converted it to Korean time (UTC+9) before deciding the quarter and month. Without this, `a_net`, `c_net`, `g_avg` and `h_growth` don't match Q2.
2. **One customer per email:** some emails belong to more than one customer ID. I counted each email as one customer, after trimming spaces and lowercasing. Without this, `b_customers`, `e_email` and `f_repeat` don't match Q2.
3. **Segment names:** the segment values had mixed case and stray spaces (e.g. `' consumer'`, `'Enterprise '`, `'SMB'`). I trimmed and lowercased them, which leaves three segments: smb, consumer and enterprise.

A few customers that share an email have different segments on their separate rows. I gave each order the segment of its own customer row, which is the version that matched Q2's `a_net`. A separate SQL query gave the same Q3 segment totals: smb 300,014,989 > consumer 291,382,587 > enterprise 261,798,754.

For h, September's net sales were 6.3% lower than August's, which is why the value is negative. The calculation script is at `/work/scripts/analyze.py`.
